You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Fennec library classes","question":"Can the coordinator report that room changes reached participants?","claims":{"A":"The workshop moved from Room 1 to Room 4.","B":"Every registered attendee received the change notice before noon.","C":"The workshop had 20 registered attendees."},"sources":{"S1":"registration ledger records 18 registered attendees.","S2":"booking ledger records the workshop move from Room 1 to Room 4.","S3":"email server accepted 18 sends and the front desk assumes receipt. The send report excludes delivery and bounce status."},"follow_up":{"S4":"independent mailbox audit finds two registered addresses first received the notice after noon."}}

message.content: {"claims":{"A":{"status":"supported","citations":["S2"],"confidence":95},"B":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S4"],"confidence":70},"C":{"status":"contradicted","citations":["S1"],"confidence":90}},"note":"Claim A is supported by the booking ledger (S2) confirming the workshop moved from Room 1 to Room 4. Claim B is contradicted by the independent mailbox audit (S4) showing two registered attendees received the notice after noon, disproving that every attendee received it before noon. Claim C is contradicted by the registration ledger (S1) recording 18 registered attendees, not 20. The email server report (S3) indicates 18 sends but lacks delivery confirmation, so it does not establish receipt."}

parsed.note: Claim A is supported by the booking ledger (S2) confirming the workshop moved from Room 1 to Room 4. Claim B is contradicted by the independent mailbox audit (S4) showing two registered attendees received the notice after noon, disproving that every attendee received it before noon. Claim C is contradicted by the registration ledger (S1) recording 18 registered attendees, not 20. The email server report (S3) indicates 18 sends but lacks delivery confirmation, so it does not establish receipt.
